sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Shortwave Radiation**: Solar energy enters the atmosphere primarily as **Shortwave (Ultraviolet/Visible)** radiation, which passes through the atmosphere with minimal absorption.
• **Longwave Radiation**: The Earth absorbs this energy and re-emits it as **Longwave (Infrared)** radiation. Greenhouse gases (GHGs) are opaque to this longwave radiation.
• **Radiative Forcing**: The measure of the influence a factor has in altering the balance of incoming and outgoing energy in the Earth-atmosphere system.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Global Warming Potential (GWP)**: A relative measure of how much heat a greenhouse gas traps in the atmosphere compared to Carbon Dioxide (CO2) over a specific time horizon (usually 100 years).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Carbon Sequestration**: Capturing and storing atmospheric CO2 through biological (afforestation) or geological (CCS) means.
• **Global Methane Pledge**: International effort to reduce methane emissions by 30% by 2030.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) conflict, economic dependence on fossil fuels.
• **Solutions**: Transition to Green Hydrogen, Carbon Pricing, and Circular Economy models.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-M-N-O-F' (Carbon, Methane, Nitrous, Ozone, Fluorinated gases).
• **Decoded Meaning**: The primary GHGs listed in the Kyoto Protocol.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Ozone' as a GHG. Remember: Tropospheric ozone is a potent GHG, while Stratospheric ozone is not (it protects from UV).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Anthropogenic Forcing' to describe human-induced climate change in your answers.

keyTakeaways: The Greenhouse Effect is a natural phenomenon; the 'Enhanced' version is the climate crisis.
GWP is the standard metric for comparing GHG impact; CO2 is the reference gas.
Methane has a higher GWP than CO2 but a shorter atmospheric lifespan, making it a 'low-hanging fruit' for immediate climate action.
